content.key_idea: ReLU activation induces sparsity in a Transformer's MLP block: only the neurons (rows/columns of FC1/FC2 weight matrices) whose activations are positive, highlighted in green and boxed in red, contribute to the output.
content.reading_order: left panel top-to-bottom: Self-Attention Block into the MLP Block (FC1, ReLU, FC2); right panel top-to-bottom: FC2 matrix multiplication above FC1 matrix multiplication, each shown as weights x input = output.

evidence: The LLM architecture includes multiple Transformer layers, each comprising a self-attention and an MLP
ReLU in this figure filters out negative values, allowing only positively valued neurons in FC1
These neurons, which contribute to the output, are considered activated in this paper.

summary: This background figure from the PowerInfer paper explains the source of activation sparsity that the system exploits. The left panel sketches a Transformer layer's MLP block: a Self-Attention Block feeds into FC1, a ReLU activation, and FC2. The right panel zooms into the matrix multiplications for FC2 (top) and FC1 (bottom), each drawn as weights x input = output, with the activated neuron rows/columns picked out in green and boxed in red against a gray background of inactive cells. The figure visually demonstrates that ReLU zeroes out negative values, so only a sparse subset of neurons in FC1 and FC2 (termed activated neurons) actually influence the output, motivating PowerInfer's hot/cold neuron distinction.
